questions.text: You need to provide real-time notifications to users about updates in a web application. Which AWS service would be most appropriate for sending notifications?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon SNS allows you to send real-time notifications to users via various communication channels, including SMS, email, and push notifications.

questions.text: For a company requiring an architecture that supports multi-region deployments with automated failover and disaster recovery for a critical application, which AWS services and strategies are best suited?

options.text: AWS Direct Connect with Amazon CloudFront, Amazon EKS, and AWS Config
Amazon S3 with AWS Snowball, Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables, and AWS Elastic Beanstalk
Amazon Route 53 with AWS Global Accelerator, Amazon Aurora Global Databases, and AWS Backup
AWS CloudFormation with AWS Lambda, Amazon RDS Multi-AZ, and AWS CloudTrail

questions.explanationHtml: Amazon Route 53 provides DNS management, AWS Global Accelerator improves performance and availability, Amazon Aurora Global Databases ensures multi-region database failover, and AWS Backup handles disaster recovery.

questions.text: For a project that involves real-time video processing and analysis, which AWS service would be most suitable?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon Kinesis Video Streams allows you to collect, process, and analyze real-time video streams, making it ideal for video processing applications.

questions.text: To monitor and receive alerts about your AWS resources‘ performance and operational status, which AWS service should you use?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon CloudWatch provides monitoring, alerting, and operational insights for AWS resources, helping track performance and set up notifications.

questions.text: To automatically scale your EC2 instances based on demand, which AWS service should you use?
questions.explanationHtml: Amazon Auto Scaling automatically adjusts the number of EC2 instances based on traffic or demand, ensuring optimal performance and cost efficiency.

questions.text: You need to implement a solution for securely transferring large volumes of data between AWS regions while maintaining data integrity and compliance. Which AWS services and features should be used?

options.text: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration with AWS Backup and Amazon RDS Multi-AZ
AWS DataSync with Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication and AWS KMS
AWS Snowcone with AWS Snowball and Amazon CloudFront
AWS Direct Connect with AWS Global Accelerator and AWS WAF

questions.explanationHtml: AWS DataSync transfers data securely and efficiently, Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication ensures data replication across regions, and AWS KMS provides encryption and compliance.

questions.text: A company wants to set up a solution for continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) with robust version control, automated testing, and deployment. Which AWS services should be used to implement this solution?

options.text: AWS Lambda with Amazon S3, AWS Step Functions, and AWS CloudFormation
AWS Fargate with AWS Elastic Beanstalk, AWS CloudTrail, and AWS CodePipeline
AWS CodePipeline with AWS CodeBuild, AWS CodeCommit, and AWS CodeDeploy
Amazon EC2 with AWS CodeDeploy, Amazon RDS, and AWS CloudWatch

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

AWS CodePipeline with AWS CodeBuild, AWS CodeCommit, and AWS CodeDeploy

This combination represents AWS’s core, purpose-built services for a CI/CD pipeline, directly matching the requirements:

  • AWS CodeCommit: Provides secure, highly scalable version control for storing code.

  • AWS CodeBuild: Automates the process of compiling source code, running tests (automated testing), and producing software packages.

  • AWS CodeDeploy: Automates code deployment to various compute services.

  • AWS CodePipeline: Orchestrates the entire CI/CD workflow, automating the stages from source code change through build, test, and deployment, providing a true continuous integration and continuous delivery solution.

Incorrect

AWS Lambda with Amazon S3, AWS Step Functions, and AWS CloudFormation

While these are powerful services for building serverless applications and infrastructure-as-code (AWS CloudFormation), this set is not the primary CI/CD service suite. AWS Step Functions is for orchestrating microservices, not for CI/CD pipelines. Amazon S3 is for storage, not version control. This combination lacks the integrated version control, build, and deployment automation of the AWS Developer Tools suite (Code services).

AWS Fargate with AWS Elastic Beanstalk, AWS CloudTrail, and AWS CodePipeline

This option mixes compute services (AWS Fargate, AWS Elastic Beanstalk) and an auditing service (AWS CloudTrail) with one CI/CD service (AWS CodePipeline). AWS CloudTrail is for API auditing and logging, not for CI/CD tasks like building or deploying code. This collection is a mismatched set of services rather than the integrated CI/CD toolchain provided by the Code* services.

Amazon EC2 with AWS CodeDeploy, Amazon RDS, and AWS CloudWatch

This option includes a compute service (Amazon EC2), a deployment service (AWS CodeDeploy), a managed database (Amazon RDS), and a monitoring service (AWS CloudWatch). It is missing critical CI/CD components like version control and a build/test service. AWS CloudWatch is for monitoring and observability, not for continuous integration. This set is incomplete for implementing a full CI/CD solution.

questions.text: Scenario: You need to set up a basic web application that will be accessed by users globally. The requirement is to ensure low latency and high availability.
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon CloudFront

  • Correct because:
    • Amazon CloudFront is a Content Delivery Network (CDN) service.
    • It caches and delivers content from edge locations worldwide, ensuring low latency for global users.
    • It also provides high availability by distributing traffic across multiple edge servers.
    • This is the best solution for a globally accessed web application where performance and availability are critical.

Incorrect

AWS Lambda

  • Incorrect because Lambda is a serverless compute service. While useful for backend logic, it does not directly ensure global low-latency delivery of web content.

Amazon RDS

  • Incorrect because RDS is a relational database service. It stores and manages data but does not deliver web content globally or reduce latency.

Amazon EC2

  • Incorrect because EC2 provides virtual servers. While you can host a web app on EC2, it does not inherently provide global distribution or latency optimization without additional services like CloudFront.

questions.text: You need to create a cost‑effective solution for hosting a high‑traffic web application with dynamic content. The solution should scale automatically with traffic spikes and provide low‑latency access to users. What combination of AWS services is most appropriate?

options.text: Utilize Amazon Lightsail for hosting, use AWS WAF for security, and Amazon S3 for backups.
Use AWS Lambda with Amazon API Gateway for dynamic content, Amazon S3 for static content, and Amazon DynamoDB for the database.
Deploy the application on AWS Fargate with Amazon ECS, use Amazon CloudFront for content delivery, and Amazon Aurora for the database.
Deploy the application on Amazon EC2 with Elastic Load Balancing, use Amazon CloudFront for caching, and Amazon RDS for the database.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

  • Use AWS Lambda with Amazon API Gateway for dynamic content, Amazon S3 for static content, and Amazon DynamoDB for the database Correct because this combination leverages serverless architecture, which is highly cost‑effective and scales automatically with traffic spikes.
    • AWS Lambda + API Gateway: Handles dynamic content requests without provisioning servers, scaling seamlessly with demand.
    • Amazon S3: Provides low‑cost, highly available storage for static content.
    • Amazon DynamoDB: Offers fully managed, serverless NoSQL database with automatic scaling and low latency. This architecture directly satisfies the exam requirements: cost‑effectiveness, scalability, and low latency.

Incorrect

  • Lightsail + WAF + S3 Incorrect because Lightsail is designed for simple, low‑traffic workloads. It does not scale automatically for high‑traffic dynamic applications. While WAF and S3 add security and backups, this option fails the scalability requirement.
  • Fargate + ECS + CloudFront + Aurora Incorrect because while this option is scalable and performant, it is more expensive than serverless solutions. Aurora and ECS introduce higher operational costs compared to DynamoDB and Lambda. This does not meet the “cost‑effective” requirement.
  • EC2 + ELB + CloudFront + RDS Incorrect because EC2 requires manual scaling or Auto Scaling Groups, which adds complexity and cost. Although CloudFront and RDS provide caching and database support, this option is not as cost‑effective as serverless.
